rows.label: Share of national-accounts growth passed to a consumption survey's mean when lining it up to a later year

source.title: World Bank, Poverty and Inequality Platform Methodology Handbook: lineup estimates
source.quote: passthrough rate of 0.7 for consumption aggregates and 1 (meaning full passthrough) for income aggregates

rows.explainer: When the World Bank carries a survey mean to a later year it passes through 0.7 of national-accounts growth per person for consumption surveys (survey consumption grows more slowly than the accounts) and all of it for income surveys. The same rule here.

rows.label: Household-survey mean as a share of national-accounts household consumption per person, United Kingdom, 2021

source.quote: SI.SPR.PCAP GBR 2021: 64.32; NE.CON.PRVT.PP.KD / SP.POP.TOTL 2021: 27894 a person; 64.32 × 365 / 27894 = 0.842

rows.explainer: How much of the national accounts' household consumption per person the household survey finds in United Kingdom (income survey, 2021), in the same 2021 PPP dollars: the shared step from a national-accounts figure to the survey scale a programme's clients are measured on (docs/normalization.md 2.12, consumption baselines). Range ±15% for the survey year and coverage.
